title: Computing optimal generalized binary split trees
formal: Is there a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm that, given rational successful-query probabilities \(p_1,\ldots,p_n\), constructs a generalized binary split tree minimizing \(\sum_{i=1}^n p_i(\operatorname{depth}_T(i)+1)\) over all correct such trees?
definitions:
The ordered keys are 1<…<n, with n≥1, p_i≥0, and sum p_i=1. Rational probabilities are binary-encoded; let B be their total encoding length. A generalized binary split tree is a rooted binary tree with exactly n nodes. Equality keys label its nodes bijectively with [n]. Each nonleaf node also has a split key in [n], which need not equal its equality key and may appear as the split key at other nodes. To search for i, first compare it for equality with the node’s equality key. On equality, stop; otherwise go left if i is less than the split key, right if i is at least the split key. A tree is correct if every key reaches its own equality node without first reaching a missing child. Even zero-probability keys must be found correctly.

Only queries equal to one of the given keys are allowed. The cost counts visited nodes, with the root at depth zero. This has the same minimizers as counting the two comparisons at each nonfinal visited node and one at the final node. The output lists child links, equality keys and split keys. Time is measured on a deterministic Turing machine, polynomial in n+B, including rational arithmetic. No approximation of optimal expected cost is requested: this is an algorithmic exact-optimization question, not a numerical benchmark asking for a single expected-cost value.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked polynomial-time construction and prove that its expected cost is no larger than that of every correct generalized binary split tree, or prove that no such algorithm exists. An NP-hardness theorem would be a conditional obstruction under P≠NP and must be labelled accordingly. Algorithms for ordinary binary search trees or unrestricted two-way comparison search trees do not settle this node model.
context:
Chrobak, Golin, Munro and Young exhibit a counterexample to the proposed Huang–Wong algorithm and invalidate its optimal-substructure argument. Thus that old claim cannot be used as an established polynomial-time solution.

Generalized split trees package an equality test and a potentially different threshold at each node. Results for other search-tree models need not transfer to this package.
why: This identifies the complexity of a basic comparison-search model whose formerly claimed polynomial algorithm was invalid.

import_provenance.original_title: Computing optimal generalized binary split trees
import_provenance.original_statement: Is there a polynomial-time algorithm for an optimal generalized binary split tree, where each node first tests equality against one key and otherwise branches using a potentially different split key? The objective is minimum expected search depth for given probabilities of successful queries.
import_provenance.supplied_caveat: Remark: The claimed 1984 polynomial-time algorithm was shown incorrect by these authors. Polynomial algorithms for ordinary two-way comparison search trees do not settle this distinct model.
